texts.text: Sunshine, the pop of tennis balls, and a crowd finding their seats. Your name is on the draw. Now you just need to register at the tournament office.
The courts are busy and the crowd is buzzing. The tournament office is by the entrance, and an old shed sits in the corner of the grounds.

blocked_text.text: A steward stops you. "Sorry, players only. Please register at the tournament office first."
The locker room is closed. The tournament has already started.
A steward stops you. "Sorry, players only. Please register at the tournament office first."
You're still in your street clothes. Get changed in the locker room first.
A steward stops you. "Sorry, players only. Please register at the tournament office first."
Not now. Get changed first, your first match starts soon.

texts.text: A small office by the entrance. A woman sits behind a desk covered in draw sheets.

effects.show_text: "Name?" The woman at the desk runs her finger down a list. "There you are." She hands you a player badge. "The group stage starts soon. You can get changed in the locker room."

The woman at the desk shakes her head. "A broken string? I'm sorry, we gave out our last spare racket this morning." She thinks for a moment. "Ask the groundskeeper. He's usually somewhere by the courts. If anyone knows where to find a racket, it's him."

actions.label: Talk to the woman at the desk

effects.show_text: "Did you find the groundskeeper? He's usually somewhere by the courts."

actions.label: Talk to the woman at the desk

texts.text: Rows of lockers and a wooden bench. It smells of fresh towels.

effects.show_text: You change into your tennis kit and check your racket one last time. The strings feel good. Time to play.

texts.text: The umpire waves you over to the net. Your next match is ready.
The court is quiet for now. Next to it, the groundskeeper is raking the clay.
The court is quiet for now.
The groundskeeper is raking the clay next to the court.

effects.show_text: The groundskeeper leans on his rake and listens. "Broken string in the group stage? Bad luck, buddy." He digs into his pocket and holds out a rusty key. "There's an old shed in the corner of the grounds. There should still be a few rackets in there."
"There should still be spare rackets in the shed."

texts.text: An old wooden shed in the corner of the grounds. The paint is peeling, and a heavy padlock hangs on the door.

blocked_text.text: You pull at the door, but the padlock won't budge. You'll need a key.

texts.text: The shed is empty now. Just old nets, ball baskets and dust.
The lock clicks open and the door creaks. Dust floats in the light. Between old nets and ball baskets, two rackets lean against the wall. One looks almost new. The other has clearly seen better days.

effects.show_text: A Wilson Blade. The grip is clean, the strings are tight, and there's barely a scratch on the frame. It looks almost new. This could be exactly what you need.

An old Yonex. The paint is chipped, the grip is worn thin, and the model name has faded completely. It doesn't look like much. You turn it in your hands, and on the side of the frame, barely readable, you make out two faded words: *Roger F.*
You take the racket. A voice crackles over the loudspeaker: "Next match starting soon!" You'd better hurry back to the courts.
You take the racket. A voice crackles over the loudspeaker: "Next match starting soon!" You'd better hurry back to the courts.

outcomes.text: You find your rhythm quickly. Clean serves, deep returns. Match won!

Your opponent is relentless. On the very last point you swing hard and hear a sharp *ping*. Your string has snapped, and the ball floats into the net. Match lost.

Thanks to your win in round 1, you're still in the tournament. But you can't play the next match without a racket.
The first points are a disaster. The old racket feels strange in your hand. But slowly, something clicks. You win, just barely. Next up: the final.
The Wilson feels light and fast in your hand. It isn't easy, but you win the match. Next up: the final.
Every shot lands exactly where you want it. Your opponent has no answer. You win the final!
In the final, nothing works. Your shots land long and your serve lets you down. You lose the final.

matches.blackout_text: On the last point, the ball hits you on the temple at full force. Everything goes dark. When you wake up, the match is over. You lost.
matches.replay_prompt: That one slipped away. Do you want to replay the match or give up?

A.title: ENDING A: The Racket of a Legend

pages.name: Award ceremony
pages.text: Confetti rains down as you lift the trophy. The crowd cheers your name.

pages.name: A stranger
pages.text: As the crowd drifts away, a stranger in a cap walks up to you. "May I take a look at that racket?" He turns it slowly in his hands, his thumb resting on the faded letters on the frame. A smile spreads across his face. "You made a good choice, kid." He hands it back, and before you can say a word, he's gone.

pages.name: Award ceremony
pages.text: You stand to the side as the winner lifts the trophy, clapping along with the crowd. So close.
